To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the black hole mass in radio-loud active galactic nuclei (AGNs) can be overestimated by the size -- continuum relation, but the black hole mass can be estimated by the size -- line luminosity relation and/or the fundamental plane relation.

(1) the BLR size of AGNs is correlated with the emission line luminosity of H$_{\beta}$, (2) the size -- continuum emission relation is not suitable to estimate the BLR size for extremely radio-loud objects, and (3) the fundamental plane relation is useful for extremely radio-lou AGNs

we present a new relation between BLR size and emission line luminosity, which can be used to obtain more accurate black hole mass of radio-loud active galactic nuclei (AGNs), and we suggest using the fundamental plane relation to estimate the black hole masses of extremely radio-loud active AGNs with weak/absence emission lines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the black hole masses in radio-loud active galactic nuclei (AGNs).
the black hole masses and their evolution in radio-loud and radio-quiet AGNs.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the size--continuum luminosity relation can be used to get black hole masses for radio-quiet AGNs and for radio-loud ones, if their host elliptical galaxies can be resolved.

the black hole masses for radio-loud and radio-quiet AGNs can be determined by using the same methods, but different methods may be needed for radio-loud or radio-quiet AGN sub-classes, depending on the observational constraints.

the size -- continuum relation can only provide the upper limit of the BLR size for radio-loud sources, and the new size -- line relation can provide the lower limit of the BLRs size, while the black hole masses can be estimated by using the new size -- luminosity relation or by using the fundamental plane relation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new approach to estimate black hole masses of AGNs with different properties, which will be very important in future AGN surveys.

, for radio-quiet AGNs with strong emission lines, we can use the BLR size -- continuum luminosities relation to estimate their black hole masses; for radio-loud and extremely radio-loud (blazar) AGNs, we can use their host galaxies' properties to estimate their black-hole masses.
the size of BLRs in radio-loud quasars is not significantly different from that in radio-quiet quasars.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BLR size -- $H_{\alpha}$ luminosity relation is more robust and less contaminated by jets, and it is more suitable for estimating the BLR sizes and black hole masses of the radio-loud AGN.
, for the first time, we can get reliable black hole masses of extremely radio-loud quasars with weak or no emission lines.

, in the absence of direct measurements, one should be very cautious when estimating black hole masses of AGNs with jets, because the jet can significantly contaminate their emission and lead to large uncertainties in the estimated black hole masses.
